tip: напишет (napishet = will write) is perfective, so its present-tense ending already means future. No быть (byt = to be) needed, and it frames writing as a single finished act.
приду (pridu = will come) is a perfective future: one word, no быть (byt = to be). обязательно (obyazatelno = definitely) fits this sense of a sure, completed arrival.
закончишь (zakonchish = will finish) is perfective, so this present-tense form points to the future. Когда (kogda = when) plus a perfective verb asks about one completed moment.
помоет (pomoyet = will wash) is perfective, so the present-tense ending carries future meaning. Завтра (zavtra = tomorrow) fits its one-time, finished sense.
решит (reshit = will solve) is perfective future, framing the task as solved once. The imperfective would be будет решать (budet reshat = will be solving), an ongoing effort.
Imperfective future is быть (byt = to be) plus an infinitive: буду слушать (budu slushat = will listen). It describes ongoing or repeated action, not one finished act.
будешь писать (budesh pisat = will write) is imperfective future and stresses the process. The perfective напишешь (napishesh) would stress finishing it.
часто покупала (chasto pokupala = often bought) is imperfective. A frequency word like часто (chasto = often) signals a repeated habit, not one purchase.
иногда готовил (inogda gotovil = sometimes cooked) is imperfective. Repeated or habitual past actions take the imperfective aspect, marked here by иногда (inogda = sometimes).
часто учила (chasto uchila = often studied) is imperfective for a repeated past habit. A single finished study would use perfective выучила (vyuchila = learned).
редко открывал (redko otkryval = rarely opened) stays imperfective. A frequency word like редко (redko = rarely) marks a repeated non-event, so the process aspect is used.
часто запечатывала (chasto zapechatyvala = often sealed) is imperfective. The -ыва- (-yva-) stem builds the repeated-action form, matching часто (chasto = often).
ходила (khodila = went on foot) is the walking verb. For going by vehicle you would say ездила (yezdila = went). English went hides this split.
сразу купил (srazu kupil = bought right away) is perfective, marking one completed act. сразу (srazu = right away) points to a finished result, so the imperfective would not fit.
сразу выучил (srazu vyuchil = learned immediately) is perfective, so the result is reached. The imperfective учил (uchil = studied) would mean was studying, with no guaranteed finish.
решал then решил (reshal, reshil): the imperfective form shows the hour-long effort, and the perfective form marks the moment it finally got solved.
писала (pisala = was writing) is imperfective and says nothing about finishing, so не дописала (ne dopisala = did not finish writing) can follow without contradiction.
искала then нашла (iskala, nashla): the imperfective describes the process of searching, and the perfective marks the successful result of finding.
весь день готовил (ves den gotovil = cooked all day) is imperfective. A time span like весь день (ves den = all day) frames the action as ongoing, so the process aspect is used.
ходили (khodili = went) here means a round trip: we went to the museum and came back. That there-and-back sense is built into the verb.
Такси (taksi = taxi) never changes form: it is indeclinable, the same in every case. Here it is the subject doing the carrying, везёт (vezyot = is taking).
поеду в Россию (poyedu v Rossiyu = will go to Russia): to show motion toward a place, use в (v = to or into) plus the accusative case.
красивее чёрной (krasiveye chyornoy = more beautiful than a black one): after a comparative, than is shown by putting the compared noun in the genitive, no extra word needed.
на море (na more = at the sea): this noun takes на (na = on or at), not в (v = in), for location. Some nouns default to на where English says at or in.
прощаемся с друзьями (proshchayemsya s druzyami = say goodbye to friends): the verb прощаться (proshchatsya) pairs with с (s = with) plus the instrumental case.
своих (svoikh = one's own) points back to the subject: о своих родителях (o svoikh roditelyakh = about her own parents), not someone else's. Use свой (svoy) when the owner is the subject.
To say about X, use о (o = about) plus the noun in -е (-e): о физике (o fizike = about physics). Before a vowel it becomes об (ob), as in об отце (ob ottse = about dad).
ждёт хозяина (zhdyot khozyaina = waits for the owner): animate masculine nouns take an -а (-a) accusative ending, identical to their genitive form.
